test_cases.test_name: Verify Continuous Temperature Monitoring and Recording Intervals
test_cases.objective: To verify that the EMS continuously monitors temperature in GMP storage areas and records readings at intervals not exceeding 5 minutes.
prerequisites: EMS system is installed and configured.
Temperature sensors are calibrated and operational in all GMP storage areas.
Access to EMS software and data logs is available.

test_steps.action: Observe the EMS interface for a continuous period of at least 15 minutes, noting the timestamp of each recorded temperature reading for a selected GMP storage area.
test_steps.expected_result: Temperature readings are continuously displayed and recorded for the selected storage area.
data_to_capture: Timestamp of each recorded temperature reading

test_steps.action: Analyze the captured data logs to determine the time difference between consecutive temperature recordings.
test_steps.expected_result: The time difference between any two consecutive temperature readings does not exceed 5 minutes.

acceptance_criteria: All temperature readings are continuously monitored and recorded.
The interval between consecutive temperature readings is consistently 5 minutes or less.
data_integrity_requirements: Data must be captured accurately and without loss.
Timestamps must be precise and reflect actual recording times.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Temperature Range, Accuracy, and Alarm Deviation
test_cases.objective: To verify that the EMS operates within the specified temperature range and accuracy, and generates alerts when temperature deviates from the setpoint.
prerequisites: EMS system is installed and configured.
Temperature sensors are calibrated and operational.
Access to EMS software and alarm configuration is available.
A calibrated reference thermometer is available for comparison.

test_steps.action: Set a target temperature within the EMS for a GMP storage area (e.g., 20°C).
test_steps.expected_result: The EMS accepts the setpoint and displays it.

test_steps.action: Using the calibrated reference thermometer, verify the actual temperature in the storage area. Compare this reading with the EMS displayed temperature.
test_steps.expected_result: The EMS displayed temperature is within ±0.5°C of the reference thermometer reading.

test_steps.action: Gradually increase or decrease the temperature in the storage area to simulate a deviation of +2°C from the setpoint (e.g., to 22°C if setpoint was 20°C).
test_steps.expected_result: The EMS generates an audible and visual alarm notification within 30 seconds.

test_steps.action: Return the temperature to within the acceptable range and acknowledge the alarm in the EMS.
test_steps.expected_result: The alarm is cleared from the EMS interface.

test_steps.action: Repeat steps 3 and 4 for a deviation of -2°C from the setpoint (e.g., to 18°C if setpoint was 20°C).
test_steps.expected_result: The EMS generates an audible and visual alarm notification within 30 seconds.

acceptance_criteria: The EMS accurately displays temperature within ±0.5°C of the reference thermometer.
The EMS generates an alarm within 30 seconds when temperature deviates ±2°C from the setpoint.
Alarms are cleared upon acknowledgment after the temperature returns to the acceptable range.
data_integrity_requirements: Temperature readings must be accurate and reflect actual conditions.
Alarm triggers and timestamps must be recorded correctly.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Vendor Software Integrity and Data Storage Format
test_cases.objective: To verify that the vendor-supplied software is used without modification and that data is stored in the vendor's standard database format.
prerequisites: Environmental Monitoring System (EMS) is installed and configured.
Access to system logs and database configuration.

test_steps.action: Access the EMS software installation directory and verify that no custom modifications have been made to the vendor-supplied files.
test_steps.expected_result: No unauthorized or custom modifications are present in the vendor-supplied software files.

test_steps.action: Query the EMS database to inspect the format of stored temperature and humidity data. Compare this format against the vendor's documentation.
test_steps.expected_result: Stored data adheres to the vendor's standard database schema and format.
data_to_capture: Sample data records from the database

acceptance_criteria: The EMS software is confirmed to be the unmodified vendor version.
The format of stored data in the database matches the vendor's specified standard.
regulatory_basis: URS-EMS-003: The system shall use vendor-supplied software without modification.
URS-EMS-006: All data shall be stored in the vendor's standard database format.
data_integrity_requirements: Data must be stored in a consistent and verifiable format.
Absence of unauthorized code modifications ensures data integrity.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Alarm Notification and System Response Time
test_cases.objective: To verify that the system generates alerts when temperature deviates from setpoint and that the system response time for alarm conditions does not exceed 30 seconds.
prerequisites: EMS is operational and monitoring temperature.
Alarm setpoints are configured.
Site paging system is accessible for verification.
Ability to simulate temperature deviations.

test_steps.action: Induce a temperature deviation in a monitored area that exceeds the ±2°C alarm threshold from the current setpoint.
test_steps.expected_result: An alarm notification is generated by the EMS.
data_to_capture: Actual temperature reading at alarm trigger

test_steps.action: Measure the time elapsed from the moment the temperature deviation occurred (as recorded by the system) to the moment the alarm notification is received by the site paging system.
test_steps.expected_result: The total system response time for the alarm condition is 30 seconds or less.
data_to_capture: Timestamp of alarm generation in EMS
Timestamp of alarm reception on paging system

test_steps.action: Verify that the alarm notification includes relevant details such as location, temperature, and time.
test_steps.expected_result: Alarm notification contains accurate and complete information.

acceptance_criteria: The EMS generates an alarm when temperature deviates ±2°C from setpoint.
The system response time for alarm conditions is within the 30-second limit.
Alarm notifications are clear and informative.
regulatory_basis: URS-EMS-005: The system shall generate alerts when temperature deviates ±2°C from setpoint.
URS-EMS-015: Alarm notifications shall integrate with site paging system using vendor API.
URS-EMS-011: System response time shall not exceed 30 seconds for alarm conditions.
data_integrity_requirements: Timely and accurate alarm generation is critical for product protection.
Verification of alarm content ensures correct response.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Audit Trail and Electronic Signature Functionality
test_cases.objective: To verify that the EMS system maintains a comprehensive audit trail and supports electronic signatures as per 21 CFR Part 11.
prerequisites: EMS system is installed and configured.
User accounts with appropriate permissions are created.
A simulated event requiring an audit trail entry (e.g., configuration change) is planned.

test_steps.action: Perform a configuration change within the EMS system (e.g., adjust a setpoint or sensor calibration).
test_steps.expected_result: An audit trail entry is created, recording the user, date, time, action performed, and the old and new values.
data_to_capture: Audit trail log entries for the performed action.

test_steps.action: Initiate an action requiring an electronic signature (e.g., approving a report or acknowledging an alarm).
test_steps.expected_result: The system prompts for and captures a valid electronic signature, including user ID, date, time, and reason for signature.
data_to_capture: Electronic signature details captured by the system.

test_steps.action: Review the audit trail and electronic signature records for completeness and accuracy.
test_steps.expected_result: All recorded events and signatures are complete, accurate, and comply with 21 CFR Part 11 requirements.
data_to_capture: Screenshots or exported reports of audit trail and electronic signature records.

acceptance_criteria: All audit trail entries are complete, accurate, and timestamped.
Electronic signatures are captured with all required components (user, date, time, reason).
Audit trail and electronic signature functionality meets 21 CFR Part 11 requirements.
data_integrity_requirements: Audit trail must be secure, unalterable, and time-stamped.
Electronic signatures must be legally equivalent to handwritten signatures.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Data Retention and Archival Functionality
test_cases.objective: To verify that the EMS system can store data for the required retention period and that the archival feature functions correctly.
prerequisites: EMS system is installed and configured.
Sufficient data has been generated to simulate a period of operation (e.g., several days or weeks).
Archival process is understood and documented.

test_steps.action: Verify the current data storage capacity and estimate the time to reach the 10-year minimum requirement.
test_steps.expected_result: The system's current storage capacity is documented, and the estimated time to reach 10 years of data is calculated.
data_to_capture: Calculated time to reach 10 years of data.

test_steps.action: Initiate the vendor's standard archival process for a defined period of historical data.
test_steps.expected_result: The archival process completes successfully, and the specified historical data is moved to the archive location.
data_to_capture: Confirmation of data moved to archive.

test_steps.action: Attempt to retrieve specific data points from the archived data.
test_steps.expected_result: The archived data is accessible and can be retrieved accurately.
data_to_capture: Confirmation of data integrity after retrieval.

test_steps.action: Verify that the system continues to log new data after archival.
test_steps.expected_result: New data is continuously logged into the active database without interruption.

acceptance_criteria: System storage capacity is sufficient for at least 10 years of continuous monitoring.
The archival process successfully moves historical data to the designated archive.
Archived data is retrievable and maintains its integrity.
Continuous data logging is maintained after archival.
data_integrity_requirements: Data must be retained for a minimum of 7 years.
Archived data must be secure, retrievable, and maintain its integrity.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Standard Report Generation for Batch Release
test_cases.objective: To verify that the Environmental Monitoring System can generate standard reports as provided by the vendor for use in batch release.
prerequisites: System is installed and configured.
Sufficient historical data exists for report generation.
Access to vendor-provided reporting tools is available.

test_steps.action: Access the reporting module of the EMS.
test_steps.expected_result: The reporting module is accessible and displays available report templates.

test_steps.action: Select a standard report template relevant to batch release (e.g., temperature log for a specific period).
test_steps.expected_result: The selected report template is loaded and ready for configuration.

test_steps.action: Configure the report parameters (e.g., date range, storage area) as per typical batch release requirements.
test_steps.expected_result: Report parameters are accepted by the system.

test_steps.action: Generate the report.
test_steps.expected_result: The report is generated successfully in the vendor's standard format.

test_steps.action: Review the generated report for accuracy and completeness of data, ensuring it aligns with recorded monitoring data.
test_steps.expected_result: The report accurately reflects the monitored data for the specified period and areas, and is suitable for batch release.
data_to_capture: Confirmation of data accuracy in the report

acceptance_criteria: Standard reports can be generated by the system.
Generated reports are in the vendor's standard format.
Reported data is accurate and complete.
Reports are suitable for use in batch release decisions.
regulatory_basis: URS-EMS-007: Standard reports provided by vendor shall be used for batch release.
data_integrity_requirements: Reported data must be a true representation of recorded data.

test_cases.test_name: Verify System Availability and Data Storage Capacity
test_cases.objective: To verify that the Environmental Monitoring System meets the specified availability percentage and has sufficient data storage capacity for the required retention period.
prerequisites: System is installed and operational.
Monitoring has been active for a significant period to assess storage usage.
Access to system logs and performance monitoring tools is available.

test_steps.action: Monitor system uptime over a defined period (e.g., 1 month) excluding planned maintenance windows.
test_steps.expected_result: The system is operational and accessible for the majority of the monitoring period.

test_steps.action: Calculate the system availability percentage based on the monitored uptime.
test_steps.expected_result: The calculated availability percentage meets or exceeds the specified requirement (99.5%).

test_steps.action: Assess the current data storage utilization.
test_steps.expected_result: Current storage utilization is within acceptable limits.

test_steps.action: Project future data storage requirements based on current usage rates and the 10-year data storage capacity requirement.
test_steps.expected_result: The projected storage requirement for 10 years is within the system's total storage capacity.
data_to_capture: Confirmation that projected requirement is less than or equal to total capacity

acceptance_criteria: System availability is >= 99.5% excluding planned maintenance.
Data storage capacity is sufficient to support a minimum of 10 years of continuous monitoring.
System logs accurately record uptime and downtime events.
regulatory_basis: URS-EMS-012: Data storage capacity shall support minimum 10 years of continuous monitoring.
URS-EMS-013: System availability shall be 99.5% excluding planned maintenance.
data_integrity_requirements: System availability ensures continuous data capture.
Sufficient storage prevents data loss due to capacity issues.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Facility Management System Integration and Alarm Notification
test_cases.objective: To verify that the EMS system successfully interfaces with the existing facility management system and integrates with the site paging system for alarm notifications.
prerequisites: EMS system is installed and configured.
Facility management system is operational.
Site paging system is operational.
Vendor API for alarm notifications is accessible.

test_steps.action: Simulate a temperature deviation that triggers an alarm condition in the EMS.
test_steps.expected_result: The EMS generates an alarm notification.

test_steps.action: Verify that the alarm notification is successfully sent to the site paging system via the vendor API.
test_steps.expected_result: An alert is received on the site paging system within the specified response time.
data_to_capture: Content of the paging system alert

test_steps.action: Verify that the EMS system logs the alarm event and its transmission to the facility management system.
test_steps.expected_result: The alarm event is recorded in the EMS audit trail, and integration logs show successful data exchange with the facility management system.
data_to_capture: Audit trail entry for the alarm

acceptance_criteria: Alarm notifications are successfully transmitted to the site paging system.
Alarm notifications are received within the specified response time (URS-EMS-011).
Integration with the facility management system is confirmed through logs.
All alarm events are logged in the EMS audit trail.
data_integrity_requirements: Audit trail entries accurately reflect alarm events and system interactions.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Data Storage Capacity and System Availability
test_cases.objective: To verify that the EMS system has sufficient data storage capacity for 10 years of continuous monitoring and meets the required system availability of 99.5%.
prerequisites: EMS system is installed and operational.
Access to system logs and monitoring tools.
Knowledge of system's data storage configuration.

test_steps.action: Review system configuration and documentation to confirm the data storage capacity settings.
test_steps.expected_result: The system configuration indicates a storage capacity sufficient for at least 10 years of continuous monitoring based on expected data generation rates.

test_steps.action: Monitor system uptime and unplanned downtime over a defined period (e.g., 1 week) to calculate availability.
test_steps.expected_result: The calculated system availability is 99.5% or higher, excluding planned maintenance periods.

test_steps.action: Simulate a scenario that might impact system availability (e.g., network interruption, server restart) and verify system recovery.
test_steps.expected_result: The system recovers within an acceptable timeframe and resumes normal operation, with minimal data loss or corruption.

acceptance_criteria: Data storage capacity is confirmed to support a minimum of 10 years of continuous monitoring.
System availability is verified to be 99.5% or greater.
System demonstrates robust recovery from simulated availability impacting events.
data_integrity_requirements: Data is not lost or corrupted during system recovery from downtime events.
Storage capacity calculations are accurate and based on realistic data generation.
